rationale: This 1970 sociological small-group experiment examines Weberian rational and legal authority within hierarchical versus autonomous group structures and their effects on simulated employee productivity and job satisfaction. It is completely unrelated to household or community water or sanitation service access (fails Criterion 1 and Criterion 4; primary exclusion code E01).
plain_vs_narrow_note: Excluded under both narrow and plain Criterion 2 readings because the study is an organizational sociology small-group experiment on supervisor authority, employee productivity and job satisfaction, with no relation to water or sanitation service access (E01).

evidence_quotes.quote: An attempt to ascertain the independent & interactional effects of autonomy-hierarchy, rational, & legal authority, on the dependent variables of job satisfaction & productivity.
Summarily, the main findings indicate that the independent variable of superior rational authority was significant in explaining variation of 'employee' productivity.
